claim_verdicts.evidence: navigations.md L10: "EF Core relationships are defined by foreign keys. Navigations are layered over foreign keys to provide a natural, object-oriented view for reading and manipulating relationships." one-to-many.md L41-44 lists the foreign key property and the reference navigation as two separate parts of one relationship (`Post.BlogId`, `Post.Blog`), and its sample dependent declares both at once. Entities.cs @ stage-1 shows the same pair on `Order`: `public int CustomerId` and `public Customer? Customer`.

one-to-many.md L86-93: "configuration of the relationships starts with `HasMany` on the principal entity type (`Blog`) and then follows this with `WithOne`. As with all relationships, it is exactly equivalent to start with dependent entity type (`Post`) and use `HasOne` followed by `WithMany`." and "Neither of these options is better than the other; they both result in exactly the same configuration." Both documented samples chain `.HasForeignKey(e => e.BlogId)`.

one-to-many.md L41-42: "Optionally, a collection navigation on the principal entity referencing the dependent entities." / "Optionally, a reference navigation on the dependent entity referencing the principal entity." L251: "Notice that the call to `WithOne` has no arguments. This is the way to tell EF that there is no navigation from `Post` to `Blog`." L349: "Notice again that `WithMany()` is called with no arguments to indicate that there is no navigation in this direction." L234 calls a one-navigation relationship "unidirectional".

keys.md L33: "You can also configure multiple properties to be the key of an entity - this is known as a composite key. Conventions will only set up a composite key in specific cases - like for an owned type collection." The Fluent API sample it links is `modelBuilder.Entity<Car>().HasKey(c => new { c.State, c.LicensePlate });` — the same anonymous-type shape as `e.HasKey(i => new { i.OrderId, i.ProductId })`.

`git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs | sed -n '25,43p'` (stage-1^{commit} = 4fca60a) diffed against the lesson's first code block: zero diff lines, character-identical. `Order` declares Id, CustomerId (int), PlacedAt, Status, Items (List<OrderItem>), Customer (`Customer?`); `OrderItem` declares only OrderId, ProductId, Quantity, UnitPriceVnd — no `Id`.

`git show stage-1:DonHang.Infrastructure/DonHangDbContext.cs | sed -n '38,57p'` diffed against the lesson's second code block: zero diff lines, indentation included. It contains `e.HasMany(o => o.Items).WithOne().HasForeignKey(i => i.OrderId);`, `e.HasOne(o => o.Customer).WithMany().HasForeignKey(o => o.CustomerId);` and `e.HasKey(i => new { i.OrderId, i.ProductId });`.

Entities.cs @ stage-1, whole file read: `Customer` declares Id, FullName, Email, City, PasswordHash only — no collection of orders; `OrderItem` declares OrderId, ProductId, Quantity, UnitPriceVnd only — no reference back to `Order`. That is exactly what the two no-argument calls `WithOne()` (line 45) and `WithMany()` (line 46) of DonHangDbContext.cs state.

Live run this session against the running stage-1 lab (localhost:8080): POST /api/v1/auth/login with `{"email":"anh.tran@example.com","password":"donhang-dev-password"}` returned a 213-char token; GET /api/v1/orders with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` returned `[{"id":1,"status":"paid","customerName":"Trần Minh Anh"},{"id":2,"status":"shipped","customerName":"Trần Minh Anh"},{"id":10,"status":"paid","customerName":"Trần Minh Anh"}]`. OrdersController.List builds `new OrderSummaryDto(o.Id, o.Status, o.Customer!.FullName)`.

one-to-many.md L63: "the reference navigation must be nullable if the foreign key property is nullable. If the foreign key property is non-nullable, then the reference navigation may be nullable or not." navigations.md L33: "Reference navigations for required relationships can be nullable or non-nullable." foreign-and-principal-keys.md L80: "the nullability of the foreign key property determines whether a relationship is optional or required. issues.quote: A[orders.customer_id] -->|HasOne + HasForeignKey, gains a second property| B[order.CustomerId + order.Customer]
issues.text: The edge label reads as if `HasOne`/`HasForeignKey` create the second property, which section 6 explicitly denies: "`orders.customer_id` existing in the database doesn't create `Order.Customer` — the C# property has to exist on the class". Per navigations.md, navigations are properties of the class that the configuration layers over a foreign key; the two calls tie existing properties to the relationship. A reader who takes the diagram literally takes away the misconception the lesson is removing.
issues.fix: Relabel the first edge so the configuration ties rather than creates, e.g. `A[orders.customer_id] -->|CustomerId + Customer declared on the class, tied by HasOne + HasForeignKey| B[order.CustomerId + order.Customer]`.

So I leave section 3 not knowing whether `HasOne`/`HasForeignKey`/`HasKey` are required or optional — and section 6 then insists the relationship has to be stated explicitly, which reads as a contradiction.
